title: SaaS Partner Integration Runbook and Onboarding Checklist
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview:
This runbook describes the recommended process, technical requirements, and escalation paths for integrating a SaaS partner with Redwood Inference. It is intended for Customer Success Managers (CSMs), Solutions Engineers (SEs), and the partner's technical teams. Use this document during the initial 60-day integration window and as an operational checklist for ongoing partner maintenance.

Goals:
- Deliver a reproducible integration that meets security and performance SLOs.
- Ensure the partner can make production calls with predictable latency and cost.
- Define clear ownership, handoffs, and escalation routes.

Audience and ownership:
- Primary: CSM (owner), Solutions Engineering (technical lead), Partner Engineering (partner-owned).
- Secondary: Support (L1), Eng-SRE (L2), Eng-Serving-Runtime (L3).

Quick summary checklist (60-day timeline):
1) Kickoff & scope alignment (Day 0–3)
   - Confirm integration scope: API patterns (text gen, embeddings, chat), expected QPS, peak concurrency, data residency requirements.
   - Collect contact matrix (names, roles, SLAs).
2) Security & compliance (Day 3–10)
   - Validate network connectivity (VPC peering, IP allowlist, TLS requirements).
   - Verify contract attachments (DPA, SOC report references) and required audits.
3) Test environment setup (Day 5–14)
   - Provision sandbox API key, scoped to partner test workspace.
   - Provide sample prompts and token/usage quotas for benchmark tests.
4) Performance validation (Day 10–30)
   - Run throughput/latency tests against expected payloads and sequence lengths.
   - Confirm autoscaling behavior and cold-start characteristics.
5) UAT & cutover (Day 30–45)
   - Partner completes UAT with real traffic patterns.
   - Schedule gradual ramp and monitor usage & errors.
6) Post-cutover review & QBR prep (Day 45–60)
   - Finalize baseline metrics and agree on QBR cadence.

Prerequisites (technical):
- Partner-side: ability to make HTTPS requests, JSON parsing, retry/backoff logic, and optional websocket support for streaming.
- Network: IP allowlist or peered VPC, outbound HTTPS to api.redwood.ai (or private endpoint).
- Auth: API keys or OAuth client credentials (for private deployments, install-specific tokens).
- Data handling: Clarify PII vs non-PII, retention windows, and encryption requirements.

Technical configuration template (sample):
- API endpoint: https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
- Authentication: Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED_KEY>
- Recommended headers: x-rw-customer-id, x-rw-environment

Sample cURL smoke test:
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer TEST_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"rw-large-1.0","input":"Hello, Redwood!","max_tokens":64}'

Performance validation checklist:
- Define representative prompt/sequence-length mix (e.g., 60% short prompts <128 tokens, 30% medium 128–512, 10% long >512).
- Run 1k request steady-state test at expected QPS. Capture p50/p95/p99 latency and token throughput.
- Validate KV cache benefits by running warm/cold cache scenarios.
- Targets: p95 latency <= 350ms for short prompts on hosted plan; p99 errors <0.5% (adjust by tier).

Security and compliance checklist:
- Confirm KMS integration details for Private deployment (customer-managed CMKs).
- Ensure audit logging is enabled and log retention meets partner requirements (enter retention policy in their contract).
- For restricted data: enable field-level redaction or on-prem option; document fields considered PII.
- MFA and SSO: require SAML SSO for admin console access on enterprise accounts.

Routing and fallback policy recommendations:
- Default routing: hosted model in closest region.
- Failure fallback: on 5xx/timeout, retry with exponential backoff up to 2 attempts, then fallback to smaller model variant or cached response.
- Cost fallback: for non-critical paths, route to quantized variant when cost/sla threshold exceeded.

Known integration pitfalls and workarounds:
- Pitfall: High variance in token length inflates latency and costs.
  Workaround: Add client-side prefiltering and token budget enforcement. Use streaming for long outputs.
- Pitfall: Unexpected 429s during bursts.
  Workaround: Implement client-side rate limiting with jitter; request Dedicated capacity if sustained high QPS.
- Pitfall: JSON-structured outputs failing strict parsers.
  Workaround: Use Redwood's structured output schema with schema-id header and validate with provided JSON Schema.

Escalation matrix (contact order):
1) Partner SE -> Redwood CSM (first 24–48 hours operational issues)
2) Redwood Support L1 (support@redwood.ai) -> triages logs and issues (within 4 business hours)
3) Eng-SRE on-call -> for incidents impacting SLOs (pagers for P1/P0)
4) Eng-Serving-Runtime -> for model runtime regressions or kernel-level bugs

Incident classification and SLA expectations:
- P0 (production down for >50% users): page Eng-SRE immediately, target TTR <2 hours.
- P1 (severe degradation): page Eng-SRE, target TTR <8 hours.
- P2 (partial impact): ticket to Support, target fix or mitigation within 72 hours.
- P3 (cosmetic): backlog grooming and triage in next sprint.

Monitoring and dashboards (must-have tiles for partner):
- Token usage by route (daily/7d/30d).
- Latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99) by model and prompt-length bucket.
- Error rate by status code and route.
- Cache hit rate and batching efficiency.
- Cost per 1k tokens vs baseline.

QBR template (recommended slides / sections):
- Executive summary (uptime, spend, actions)
- Usage and growth (top routes, peak concurrency)
- Performance (latency/SLO adherence, regressions)
- Cost and optimization opportunities (quantization, batching)
- Security & compliance updates (audit findings, open items)
- Roadmap / upcoming changes (model upgrades, infra migrations)
- Action items and owners (RACI for next quarter)

Post-onboarding handoff checklist:
- Confirm monitoring dashboards live and shared with partner.
- Transfer runbooks to partner Confluence space if requested.
- Schedule first operational QBR within 30 days of cutover.
- Set recurring support review cadence (monthly for first quarter, then quarterly).

Appendix A — Example alert thresholds:
- error_rate(route) > 1% over 5m -> severity P1
- p95_latency(model,short_prompts) > 500ms over 10m -> severity P1
- token_spend_day change > 30% day-over-day -> notify CSM

Appendix B — Example integration manifest (for partner config):
{"partner_id": "partner-acme", "environments": ["sandbox","production"], "endpoints": {"sandbox": "https://sandbox.api.redwood.example/v1", "production": "https://api.redwood.example/v1"}, "contact": {"technical": "eng+acme@partner.com", "business": "biz+acme@partner.com"}, "qps_expectation": "50", "data_sensitivity": "non-PII"}

Appendix C — Useful links and references:
- Developer quickstart: https://playground.redwood.ai/quickstart
- API reference: https://docs.redwood.ai/api
- Security & compliance overview: https://intranet.redwood.ai/security/compliance
- Support portal (create ticket): https://support.redwood.ai

If you have additions or local variations for a specific partner vertical (healthcare, finance, government), create a sibling page using this runbook as the template and label it with the vertical tag.
